title: WariVerse — can we still see the Wari?
description: The board is ordered by the question it answers, not by which service produced the metric. Row 1 is the only row that matters at 2 a.m.: can the control room see the crowd. Rows 2 and 3 are the API and the operational load, which are what you look at once you know the answer to row 1 is yes.

panels.title: Can we see? — read this row first
Cameras online
panels.description: Against total configured. Anything below total means one or more zones are estimating rather than measuring.

panels.title: Oldest zone reading
panels.description: The single most important number on this board. It is the age of the STALEST zone, not an average — an average hides one dark corridor behind thirty-nine healthy ones. Above 300s the console renders that zone as UNKNOWN.

panels.title: Reading age per zone
panels.description: A sawtooth is healthy — each tooth is a fresh reading resetting the age. A line that climbs and does not come back down is a zone that has gone dark, and the density figure beside it has stopped meaning anything.

panels.title: Density per zone (p/m²)
panels.description: No alert fires on this panel, deliberately. A dense zone is Tuesday of the Wari and the product already routes it to an operator with a recommended action. Paging an engineer for it would train them to silence the pager that also tells them the cameras died.

panels.title: Stagnation index per zone
panels.description: The technical insight of the project, on a panel. Stagnation rises BEFORE density in a crush precursor — a dense crowd that has stopped moving is the dangerous state, and this line turns up first. Watch it against the density panel beside it.

panels.title: Reading confidence per zone
panels.description: Below 1.0 the density figure is an estimate rather than a measurement — usually because the zone has lost a camera. Section 0 rule 3: no AI output is presented as certainty, and that applies to the dashboard too.

panels.title: Alerts raised
panels.description: By type. A flat line during a busy afternoon is more suspicious than a spike — it usually means ingest stopped rather than that the crowd behaved.

panels.title: Request latency p95 by route
panels.description: Section 11: p95 < 300ms. The threshold line is the target, not a suggestion. During a release window the contended write is POST /passes; everything else should be flat.

panels.title: Request rate by status class
panels.description: 5xx is the only series that should ever be zero. A rising 4xx during a release window is the slot ledger correctly refusing a full slot — that is the system working, not failing.

panels.title: Passes issued / scanned / reslotted
panels.description: Scans well below issues over a slot window is a no-show rate, which is what the reslotting job reads. A reslot spike means the gate is running behind its plan.

panels.title: Open alerts by severity / SLA breaches
panels.description: SLA breaches are a control-room staffing signal, not an engineering one. Escalate them to the duty officer.

panels.title: Dindis reporting vs silent
panels.description: Fourteen dots on a map means nothing without 'and six more groups are walking that we cannot see'. When silent overtakes reporting, the halt-town board is guessing.

panels.title: Assistant turns by outcome
panels.description: The outcomes mean opposite things. Rising no_data is an outage. Rising refused is a product telling users the wrong thing about what the assistant is for. Rising degraded means the model has been unreachable and nobody noticed — the fallback works well enough to hide it.
